texts.facts: The lead suit has been suit no. CS87/2007, titled 'Subhash Chand Goel Vs. General Mills India Pvt. Ltd.' The other suit no. CS196/2007 is the counter claim of defendant. 2. The brief facts of the lead case (C.S. No. 87/2007) are as follows. The defendant was inducted as a tenant by the plaintiff in respect of the basement and ground floor (area measuring approximately 4200 sq. ft.) at I2150, DSIDC, Narela, New Delhi on a monthly rent of CS No.87/2007 Subhash Chand Goel Vs. General Mills India Pvt. Ltd. Rs.32,000/ payable on or before 8th of every month by cheque by defendant. The tenancy was for a period of 11 months w.e.f. 01.01.2006. The rent was duly paid against receipt till October 2006. The tenanted premises was used as a ware house by the defendant to store its goods. Defendant had agreed to pay electricity charges as per actual consumption @ Rs. 5.20 per unit. The defendant had agreed and undertook to keep the tenanted premises in good condition, not to cause or let the premises suffer any damage thereto and deliver back vacant premises to plaintiff on termination of tenancy period in the same condition in which it was let out. The tenancy premises were handed over by plaintiff to defendant in excellent condition as it was newly constructed having "A" grade building construction and electrical fittings having separate circuit and MCV's. Earlier, the defendant was also the tenant in the basement of said premises for 11 months from December 2004 to October 2005 and had no complaints. The building was also having fire extinguishers at all the floors. At around 1.30 a.m. on the intervening night of 28/29.10.2006, a fire broke out in the tenancy premises. Neighbours called fire brigade. Plaintiff was informed by the Agent/Manager of the defendant at 9.00 a.m. on 29.10.2006. Plaintiff CS No.87/2007 Subhash Chand Goel Vs. General Mills India Pvt. Ltd. immediately reached the ) C.S. No.87/2007 vs General Mills India Pvt. Ltd on 30 April, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108381548/ 2 premises and remained there till the fire brigade put off the fire at around 3.30 p.m. The fire broke in the tenanted portion due to negligence of defendant and had caused extensive damages to the said premises consisting of basement, ground floor and vacant first floor. Plaintiff asked the Manager/Agent of the defendant for payment of the damages caused to the building by the fire, who stated that he would assess the amount of damages caused to the building by the fire and send the assessment and amount required for restoration/repair of the premises to his head office assuring the proposal would be sanctioned as assessed/proposed by him or premises would be restored to its original position by the defendant itself. Said promise was not kept by defendant despite reminders and assurances and service of legal notices dated 04.11.2006 and 05.12.2006. Survey was got conducted by plaintiff from Sh. Sanjeev Arya, Engineer and Architect for rehabilitation/restoration/ repair of fire affected building/premises, who has estimated the cost of restoration/rehabilitation to the tune of Rs. 12,25,725/. Since, neither defendant restored the tenanted premises to original condition nor paid the aforesaid demanded sum of Rs. 12,25,725/ nor paid the arrears of rent from November 2006 to December 2006, present suit was filed by CS No.87/2007 Subhash Chand Goel Vs. General Mills India Pvt. Ltd. plaintiff claiming (i) damage of Rs. 12,25,725/ to the building caused; (ii) Rs. 25,000/ paid to Architect/Engineer; (iii) Rs. 25,000/ paid to Advocate for legal services; (iv) Rs. 25,000/ for electricity charges from beginning of tenancy till the premises was abandoned/deserted by the defendant for 4810 units @ 5.20 per unit; (v) Rs. 72,000/ as arrears of rent from November 2006 to December 2006 @ Rs. 32,000/ per month besides the damages for denial of rental income from basement and ground floor and of first floor after December 2006 @ Rs. 15,000/ per month or as per the inquiry and assessment of the Court alongwith interest @ 24% per annum till realization. Plaintiff has also prayed for decree of mandatory injunction against defendant, seeking direction to defendant to restore the building to its original position in which it was let out. 3. In the written statement filed by defendant preliminary objections were taken as (i) the suit is misconceived and baseless; (ii) the tenanted premises were taken by defendant for purpose of using it as warehouse for storage of food items sold by defendant and while entering into lease, plaintiff assured defendant that the said property was free from CS No.87/2007 Subhash Chand Goel Vs. General Mills India Pvt. Ltd. all defects and the wiring installed in the said property was the best and defendant would not have any problem with regard to the usage of said property but no fire safety equipments were installed therein nor ever installed during tenancy period; (iii) at no point of time any combustible or hazardous goods were stored in the tenanted premises by the defendant; (iv) the defendant after taking the premises on rent did not carry out any changes either in the structure or in the electrical fittings installed in the tenanted premises; (v) when the fire broke out on the fateful night, neither any representative of defendant was present at the warehouse nor the warehouse was open nor any combustible or hazardous goods were stored in the warehouse. The only probable cause was due to short circuit in the faulty/poor quality wiring installed at the premises, which had been got installed by the plaintiff himself since defendant had not carried out any wiring in the tenanted premises; (vi) defendant also averred that it was the plaintiff, who was liable to pay damages for loss incurred by the defendant on account of such gross negligent and callous approach of plaintiff, which damages have been claimed by way of a counter claim registered ) C.S. No.87/2007 vs General Mills India Pvt. Ltd on 30 April, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108381548/ 3 as C.S. No. 196/2007. CS No.87/2007 Subhash Chand Goel Vs. 4. Plaintiff filed replication to written statement of the defendant to controvert the contentions of the written statement and to reiterate the averments of the plaint. 5. In counter claim registered as CS No. 196/2007, defendant prayed for decree of Rs. 18,13,000/ against respondent/plaintiff with interest @ 24% per annum alleging due to faulty/poor quality wires installed in the tenanted premises, noninstallation of fire safety equipments by plaintiff/landlord and not insuring premises by landlord, defendant/counter claimant suffered loss and goods worth approximately Rs. 40 Lakh, which goods of counter claimant were damaged/destroyed due to negligence of plaintiff. Besides that the counter claimant claimed Rs. 8 Lakh towards loss of business profits which it would have earned in the normal course of business had the goods been sold as fit for human consumption but for the acts of callous and negligence on the part of the plaintiff, counter claimant/defendant lost 66491 Kgs of material worth approximately Rs.40 Lakh and loss of profits of Rs. 8 Lakh. Counter claimant also alleged that after the fire, they started removing stock of goods from warehouse and initially goods damaged due to fire were CS No.87/2007 Subhash Chand Goel Vs. Mills India Pvt. Ltd. removed . On 02.11.2006, the plaintiff/landlord forcibly locked the premises, did not permit the representative of counter claimant/defendant to further remove the damaged stocks and the tenanted premises were put under his own lock and key by plaintiff/landlord. Even, later representatives of counter claimant/defendant were not permitted by the plaintiff/landlord to take out the damaged material and plaintiff/landlord threatened that he would sell the goods lying in the premises. Plaintiff/landlord got a legal notice dated 04.11.2006 issued through counsel calling upon counter claimant/defendant either to repair or to inter alia pay a sum of Rs. 5 Lakh towards cost of restoration of the tenanted premises. Even on 14.11.2006, representatives of counter claimant/defendant were not permitted to remove the damaged goods by plaintiff/landlord. Again on 05.12.2006, another legal notice was got issued by plaintiff/landlord to pay a sum of Rs. 12,25,725/ as cost of restoration of the premises. Counter claimant by its letter dated 08.12.2006 had called upon plaintiff/landlord notifying the circumstances in which it had to leave the premises forcibly and terminated the tenancy and also called upon the plaintiff/landlord to refund the balance amount of advance money after adjusting the rent for the month of November CS No.87/2007 Subhash Chand Goel Vs. General Mills India Pvt. Ltd. 2006. Counter claimant/defendant replied to legal notice dated 05.12.2006 vide its letter dated 18.12.2006 denying the allegations of the notice requesting premises be made available for inspection of the premises by the Architect of Counter claimant to assess the damages, if any, caused to the premises. Plaintiff/respondent sent reply dated 23.12.2006 making false allegations which were denied by counter claimant/defendant vide letter dated 30.12.2006, again seeking plaintiff to fix an appointment to inspect the premises but despite calling of defendant/counter claimant, the plaintiff/landlord refused to open the premises for inspection. Defendant had to lodge complaints dated 09.12.2006 and 18.12.2006 with local police station to ensure that the plaintiff/landlord does not sell the damaged stock of defendant/counter claimant in the open market as consumable goods. Accordingly, the green giant stock of goods worth Rs. 10 Lakh could not be removed from the tenanted premises by defendant/counter claimant/tenant which was in the power and possession of plaintiff/landlord, who started demanding arbitrary sums without even disclosing what actual ) C.S. No.87/2007 vs General Mills India Pvt. Ltd on 30 April, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108381548/ 4 damage premises had suffered. Counter claimant was not aware what happened to the said green giant stock and has accordingly prayed for grant of decree of CS No.87/2007 Subhash Chand Goel Vs. Pvt . Ltd. mandatory injunction , seeking direction to plaintiff/landlord to release the green giant stock of goods, which had got damaged due to wetting during the fire fighting operations and was in the power and possession of plaintiff/landlord or in the alternative in case plaintiff/landlord had parted with the stock or the stock was sold in the market, then plaintiff/landlord to be directed to deposit the sale proceeds and also to pass decree of Rs. 18,13,000/ in favour of counter claimant and against plaintiff/landlord with interest @ 24% per annum. 6. The plaintiff/respondent/landlord filed written statement to counter claim of counter claimant/defendant alleging it being not maintainable, neither signed nor verified by any authorized person nor supported by any relevant documents, being vague, bogus, false, frivolous and counter claimant having concealed material facts and put forth a bunch of lies. Plaintiff alleged premises were handed over to counter claimant in excellent condition fitted with proper safety measures and the fire broke out due to the gross negligence of the counter claimant, which damaged premises very b a d l y . General Mills India Pvt. Ltd. counter claimant was inducted as a tenant in the basement of tenanted premises from December 2004 to October 2005, about the condition of the premises. The portions underneath the staircase in basement and one room at ground floor were converted into offices where computer, printer, heater/electric gadgets were installed by counter claimant who even made electrical and structural changes in the tenanted premises. The plaintiff alleged counter claimant/defendant had removed all stocks of damaged goods from the warehouse at once initially, which was not left there after fire but filed forged complaints against plaintiff for not allowing counter claimant/defendant to remove the left damaged goods and it was counter claimant/defendant, who locked the premises. Plaintiff also reiterated the averments of his plaint in the reply of counter claim denying claims of counter claimant/defendant or any negligence on own part. 7. Counter claimant filed replication to written statement of respondent/landlord to controvert the objections of the written statement and to reiterate the averments of the counter claim. 8. Admission/denial was done by parties through counsel on 15.11.2007 before my Ld. Predecessor, whereof defendant admitted six documents of plaintiff viz. (i) lease agreement dated 15.12.2004 exhibited as Ex P1; (ii) lease agreement dated 01.01.2006 exhibited as Ex P2; (iii) letter of defendant dated 14.11.2006 exhibited as Ex P3; (iv) letter of defendant dated 08.12.2006 exhibited as Ex P4; (v) reply of defendant dated 18.12.2006 exhibited as Ex P5 and (vi) letter of defendant dated 30.12.2006 exhibited as Ex P6. Plaintiff did not admit any of the documents of defendant. Plaintiff also relied upon the documents i.e. (i) copy of letter dated 22.11.2006 issued by Delhi Fire Service exhibited as Ex PW1/2; (ii) copy of legal notice dated 04.11.2006 exhibited as Ex PW1/3; (iii) postal receipts exhibited as Ex PW1/4; (iv) UPC exhibited as Ex PW1/5; (v) AD Cards exhibited as Ex PW1/6 and 7, respectively; (vi) copy of legal notice dated 05.12.2006 exhibited as Ex PW1/8 (colly); (vii) postal receipts, UPC, AD Cards exhibited as Ex PW1/9, 10, 11 and 12, respectively; (viii) copy of the reminder legal notice exhibited as Ex PW 1/13 and (ix) Fax receipt CS No.87/2007 Subhash Chand Goel Vs. General Mills India Pvt. Ltd. exhibited as Ex PW1/14. PW1 and PW2 have been crossexamined on behalf of defendant. Vide order dated 19.11.2012 my Ld. Predecessor ordered segregation of file of counter claim, which was segregated. Despite several opportunities, partly examined DW1 did not again enter into witness box for cross examination. My Ld. Predecessor closed defendant evidence vide order dated 15.11.2014 with the observation that the affidavit of DW1 filed by defendant would not be read in evidence. Part testimony of DW1 cannot be read in evidence. ) C.S. No.87/2007 vs General Mills India Pvt. Ltd on 30 April, 2015 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108381548/ 6 11.
